hot_window_recommendation.recommended_hot_window: 90 days minimum, with the live full-table aggregate in main.py's /api/transfer-graph/stats being the actual binding constraint, not any single consumer's individual time filter.
reasoning: The overwhelming majority of REAL consumer query shapes (dev_intelligence_v3, launch_wave_detection, master_launch_score, dev_intelligence_v3_enhancements) are RECENT_ONLY, bounded to 24h/72h/7d windows — these would be fully served by a HOT window far shorter than 90 days.

graph_dev_farm_detection.py / dev_intelligence_graph.py's WalletGraphBuilder explicitly parameterizes days_back with an observed default of 90 days in its docstring example — this is the single longest EXPLICIT time-bounded window found among real (non-synthetic) consumers.

src/core/storage_monitoring.py's own synthetic latency probe uses a 90-day retention_window benchmark, independently corroborating 90 days as the design-intended retention boundary already baked into this codebase (predates this P4 pass).

The hardest constraint is main.py's api_transfer_graph_stats full aggregate (COUNT/MIN/MAX/DISTINCT over the WHOLE unbounded table) — this is a LIVE endpoint, but its own 5-minute TTL cache means it is NOT latency-critical on every request; it can tolerate hitting HOT+COLD together via UnifiedTransferReader (already designed for exactly this in transfer_cold_store.py/unified_transfer_reader.py) once every 5 minutes, rather than requiring the full 5.2M rows to live in HOT permanently. This decouples the 'needs full history' requirement from 'needs it in HOT'.

wallet_clustering.py's full_rebuild is unbounded/full-scan by its own docstring, but the module already implements an incremental rowid-cursor mode for the common case, meaning full-table access is a rare/manual operation, not the steady-state — acceptable to serve from HOT+COLD via the unified reader rather than requiring HOT to hold everything.

second_hop_builder.py and funder_overlap_analysis.py / launch_prediction_engine.py / advanced_farm_intelligence_engine.py all run unbounded amount-filtered (not time-filtered) full scans as BATCH/OFFLINE jobs — these need full historical coverage but are NOT live-latency-sensitive, so they are the correct candidates to route through the cross-tier UnifiedTransferReader rather than driving the HOT window size upward.

CONCLUSION: HOT window = 90 days (covers every live/near-live query path directly, matches the pre-existing 90-day design signal in storage_monitoring.py's probe) + the PINNED rows from Task 2 (regardless of age) + route the handful of genuinely-unbounded batch/offline analytical jobs through the already-designed UnifiedTransferReader (src/ops/unified_transfer_reader.py) so they keep working transparently against HOT+COLD without requiring COLD data to ever re-enter HOT.
